evidence: Caes. B.C. 1.25: faucēs portūs angustissimae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Narrow, and so small, cramped (domus angusta); of means, scanty (rēs angustae); of the mind, petty (angustī animī, narrow-minded, Traupman 349). angustiae are a narrow pass and, figuratively, straits, difficulties (Lewis & Short).
Fitted close: tight bonds and embraces, narrow confined spaces; artē, closely, tightly. Not to be confused with artus, artūs, a joint or limb.

phrases.latin: omnis enim fermē via praeceps, angusta, lūbrica erat
phrases.english: for nearly the whole way was steep, narrow and slippery

phrases.latin: saepius et tēctīs penetrālibus extulit ōva angustum formīca terēns iter
phrases.english: and more often the ant, wearing a narrow track, has carried her eggs out of her inner chambers

phrases.latin: quaesō, tam angustam tālis vir pōnis domum?
phrases.english: please, are you, a man like you, building so cramped a house?
